title: Nullifying the Height — Straw, Dirt, and a Sagging Sukkah
subtitle: Which floor-fillers actually lower an over-height sukkah, then a run of measurement edge-cases: hanging branch-tips, raised platforms, and curved walls.
sources: Gemara text: Sefaria (William Davidson Edition). Structure and quiz questions 1-3 cross-checked against the Dafyomi Advancement Forum (dafyomi.co.il) quiz for Sukkah 4. Tosfos: dafyomi.co.il's "Point by Point Summary of Tosfos" (Yaakov Montrose, Kollel Iyun Hadaf).
before: 3b ended on a teaser: does piling cushions and blankets on the sukkah floor count as lowering an over-height sukkah? This amud opens with the answer — no, and explains why — then works through which floor-fillers do count.

From there the Gemara runs through a series of measurement edge-cases that all lean on the same idea used back on 3a-3b: a wall (or something that can stand in for one) can be a little short of reaching where you'd expect, and the gap gets treated as if it weren't there. Watch for that same move showing up in several different disguises.

flow.label: Cushions and blankets don't lower an over-height sukkah
flow.sub: even if you declare you won't use them again — no one actually treats bedding that way, so the declaration doesn't count

flow.label: What does count as a real reduction?

flowCaption: One nullification rule, then a run of platform/height edge-cases all leaning on the same "close enough counts" move.

opinions.claim: Straw left on the floor with no plan to remove it is automatically treated like nullified dirt — no explicit declaration needed.
opinions.basis: A kal v'chomer from the parallel Mishnah in Oholot: if plain dirt needs no declaration, straw left indefinitely needs none either.

opinions.claim: Straw left without a plan to remove it, and plain dirt with no stated intent, are not automatically nullified — only an explicit declaration lowers the sukkah's height.
opinions.basis: Inferred from the Mishnah in Oholot's requirement of active nullification.

opinions.claim: Thought the same rule that validates a >20-amos sukkah with low-hanging shade-giving branch-tips should also validate a <10-tefachim sukkah where low branch-tips let in more sun than shade.
opinions.basis: A symmetry argument from the >20-amos case.

opinions.claim: Rejects Abaye's symmetry: branches sagging down into the 10-tefachim minimum make it a "sagging residence" (dirah serucha) — not a livable dwelling at all, so it can't count as dirat arai regardless of the shade math.
opinions.basis: A conceptual objection, not a textual one — some things fail before the math even applies.

script.speaker: Gemara explains
script.gloss: Even if one nullifies the cushions and blankets — declaring he won't use them for anything else — that doesn't count, because his intention is overridden by how everyone else actually behaves. People don't really treat bedding that way, so the declaration is discounted.

script.speaker: Gemara continues
script.gloss: Straw placed on the floor and formally nullified is a real reduction — its status becomes like dirt. All the more so if it's dirt that was nullified.

script.speaker: Gemara raises a case
script.gloss: What about straw left with no plan to ever remove it (but not formally nullified), or plain dirt placed with no stated intent at all? This is a machloket between Rabbi Yosei and the Rabbis.

script.speaker: Gemara cites the source
script.quote: בַּיִת שֶׁמִּילְּאָהוּ תֶּבֶן אוֹ צְרוֹרוֹת וּבִיטְּלוֹ — מְבוּטָּל.
script.gloss: From a parallel Mishnah (Oholot): a house filled with straw or pebbles and then nullified — the nullification takes effect (relevant there for how tzaraat-impurity spreads through a roof).

script.speaker: Rabbi Yosei's beraita
script.quote: תֶּבֶן וְאֵין עָתִיד לְפַנּוֹתוֹ — הֲרֵי הוּא כְּעָפָר סְתָם, וּבָטֵל. עָפָר וְעָתִיד לְפַנּוֹתוֹ — הֲרֵי הוּא כִּסְתַם תֶּבֶן, וְלָא בָּטֵיל.
script.gloss: Rabbi Yosei: straw with no plan to remove it is treated like unstated dirt — nullified automatically. Dirt that he does plan to remove is treated like unstated straw — not nullified.

script.speaker: New case
script.quote: הָיְתָה גְּבוֹהָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה וְהוּצִין יוֹרְדִין בְּתוֹךְ עֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה, אִם צִלָּתָם מְרוּבָּה מֵחֲמָתָם — כְּשֵׁרָה, וְאִם לָאו — פְּסוּלָה.
script.gloss: If the sukkah is over 20 amos high but the tips of palm-branch sechach hang down within 20 amos: valid if the shade from just those low tips outweighs the sun; otherwise invalid.

script.speaker: Abaye's attempted symmetry
script.quote: סָבַר אַבָּיֵי לְמֵימַר אִם חֲמָתָם מְרוּבָּה מִצִּלָּתָם — כְּשֵׁירָה.
script.gloss: Abaye thought the mirror case should work too: a sukkah under 10 tefachim where low-hanging tips let in more sun than shade should still be valid.

script.speaker: Rava rejects it
script.quote: הָא דִּירָה סְרוּחָה הִיא, וְאֵין אָדָם דָּר בְּדִירָה סְרוּחָה.
script.gloss: Rava: that's a "sagging residence" — no one actually lives in a sagging residence, so it fails as a dwelling before the shade-calculation even matters.

script.speaker: Platform opposite the middle wall
script.quote: הָיְתָה גְּבוֹהָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה וּבָנָה בָּהּ אִיצְטְבָא כְּנֶגֶד דּוֹפֶן הָאֶמְצָעִי... וְיֵשׁ בָּהּ הֶכְשֵׁר סוּכָּה — כְּשֵׁרָה.
script.gloss: If a sukkah over 20 amos has a raised platform built opposite the middle wall, big enough on its own to count as a minimal sukkah, it's valid — that platform-to-roof section forms its own small kosher sukkah.

script.speaker: Platform along a side wall
script.quote: וּמִן הַצַּד, אִם יֵשׁ מִשְּׂפַת אִיצְטְבָא לַכּוֹתֶל אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת — פְּסוּלָה, פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת — כְּשֵׁרָה.
script.gloss: If the platform runs along a side wall instead: invalid if the gap from platform-edge to wall is 4 amos or more; valid if under 4 amos — the roofing over that gap is treated as a curved extension of the wall.

script.speaker: Gemara asks
script.quote: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, דְּאָמְרִינַן דּוֹפֶן עֲקוּמָּה?
script.gloss: What's new here? We already know the "curved wall" (dofen akuma) principle from the earlier mishnah about a breached, re-roofed house (17a) — same 4-amos threshold.

script.speaker: Gemara answers
script.quote: הָתָם הוּא דְּחַזְיָא לְדוֹפֶן, אֲבָל הָכָא... אֵימָא לָא, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
script.gloss: You might have thought curved-wall only works where the existing wall was already fit to be a sukkah-wall (as in the breached-house case) — not here, where the far wall is too tall on its own to ever be a valid sukkah-wall. This teaches that it still works.

script.speaker: Platform in the center
script.quote: הָיְתָה גְּבוֹהָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה וּבָנָה אִיצְטְבָא בְּאֶמְצָעִיתָהּ, אִם יֵשׁ מִשְּׂפַת אִיצְטְבָא וְלַדּוֹפֶן אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת לְכׇל רוּחַ וָרוּחַ — פְּסוּלָה, פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת — כְּשֵׁרָה.
script.gloss: A platform in the very center: invalid if the gap to the wall is 4 amos or more in any direction; valid only if under 4 amos on every side.

script.speaker: Gemara asks again
script.quote: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן... הַיְינוּ הָךְ!
script.gloss: Same question — isn't this identical to the side-wall case just taught?

script.speaker: Gemara answers
script.quote: דּוֹפֶן עֲקוּמָּה מֵרוּחַ אַחַת — אָמְרִינַן, אֲבָל כׇּל רוּחַ וָרוּחַ — לָא, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
script.gloss: You might have thought curved-wall only applies on one side — not on all four sides of a fully-open center platform. This teaches that it applies all around.

script.speaker: Looking ahead
script.quote: הָיְתָה פְּחוּתָה מֵעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, וְחָקַק בָּהּ כְּדֵי לְהַשְׁלִימָהּ לַעֲשָׂרָה, אִם יֵשׁ מִשְּׂפַת חֲקָק וְלַכּוֹתֶל שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים — פְּסוּלָה.
script.gloss: New case, cliffhanging into 4b: a sukkah under 10 tefachim, where a pit is dug into the floor to reach the 10-tefachim minimum. If the gap from the pit's edge to the wall is 3 tefachim or more, it's invalid — continued on 4b.

tosfos.summary: Why pillows aren't nullified the way money purses sometimes are.

points.label: (a) Implied Question
points.he: לא דמי לארנקי דפ׳ חלון (עירובין דף עט.)
points.en: This is unlike the case of a money purse discussed in Eruvin (79a). Why not?

points.label: (b) Answer
points.he: דאיכא למאן דאמר דאפילו ארנקי מבטל איניש
points.en: There's an opinion that people do nullify even money purses (unlike pillows, which people never really treat as disposable).

tosfos.summary: The correct text of the parallel Mishnah in Oholot, and why our Gemara can apply it to straw even though the Mishnah itself never mentions straw.

points.label: (a) Text
points.he: כך היא הגירסא בכל הספרים כאן
points.en: This is the text in all the manuscripts here.

points.label: 1. Text (cont.)
points.he: ובפרק חלון... והיא משנה במסכת אהלות פט״ו ולא כתב שם תבן אלא עפר או צרורות
points.en: In Eruvin (78b) the same Mishnah (Oholot 15:7) is quoted about a straw-filled ditch between two courtyards — but the Mishnah itself only says "earth or pebbles," never "straw." A copying error apparently crept "straw" into some texts.

points.label: (b) Implied Question
points.en: One can't say what's quoted here is a Beraita rather than this Mishnah. Why not?

points.label: (c) Answer
points.he: דאין לו להביא מן הברייתא כיון שיכול להביא מן המשנה
points.en: Because the Gemara wouldn't cite a Beraita when it could cite the Mishnah directly.

points.label: (e) Implied Question
points.he: והא דקאמר תבן ואין עתיד לפנותו... אף על גב דבמתניתין דאהלות לא איירי רבנן מידי בתבן
points.en: Our Gemara treats the straw case as the Rabbi Yosei/Rabbanan machloket — but the Mishnah in Oholot never actually discusses straw at all. How can the Gemara extend the machloket there?

points.label: (f) Answer
points.he: מכ״ש הוא דידע ליה כיון דבעפר וצרורות מצרכי רבנן ביטול כ״ש בתבן
points.en: It's a kal v'chomer: if the Rabbanan require nullification even for dirt and pebbles, they certainly require it for straw.

points.label: (h)-(i) Implied Question & Answer
points.he: והא דקאמר עפר סתם מחלוקת רבי יוסי ורבנן... אלא משום ר׳ יוסי נקט עפר סתם
points.en: Why does the Gemara frame the machloket around "unstated dirt" specifically, rather than also spelling out "straw with no plan to remove it"? Because the case is really built around Rabbi Yosei's position — he holds even unstated dirt is nullified automatically, and the Gemara didn't bother spelling out every parallel case.

tosfos.summary: Why hanging branch-tips validate a sukkah here, when a similar case in Eruvin invalidates it.

points.label: (a) Question
points.he: וא״ת כשצלתו מרובה מחמתו אמאי כשרה הא אי קלשת היו ההוצין נופלין
points.en: If you removed the higher sechach, wouldn't the remaining low branch-tips just fall down on their own (being too sparse to hold together)? Why is the sukkah valid at all then?

points.label: 1. Proof
points.he: כדאשכחן בעירובין (דף ג.) גבי מקצת סכך בתוך כ׳...
points.en: This mirrors Eruvin (3a): where some sechach is within 20 amos and some above, removing the higher part would leave more sun than shade — because the remaining sechach is too sparse to survive on its own; the wind would scatter it.

points.label: (b) Answer
points.he: ויש לומר דהכא יש לנו להכשיר יותר שיש רוב הוצין וראויין הן להתקיים בקל
points.en: Here there's more reason to validate it — there are enough branch-tips that they could easily hold together on their own, given something to lean on.
